hero.label: Kraków → Prague
hero.intro: Kraków to Prague by private chauffeur is a 385 km door-to-door transfer west through Silesia and across Moravia, around four hours of driving. Prestigo’s fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes-Benz E-Class, Polish motorway tolls and the Czech vignette included. Pickup from any Kraków address, Kraków Główny or Kraków Airport (KRK), drop-off anywhere in Prague.
hero.imageAlt: Private chauffeur transfer from Kraków to Prague in a Mercedes

openingParagraphs: A private transfer from Kraków to Prague covers about 385 km — west on the A4 toll motorway past Katowice, over the Czech border near Ostrava, then the D1 motorway across Moravia to Prague — and takes around four hours door to door. The fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers; groups of up to 6 travel in the V-Class from €{vPrice}; the S-Class is available from €{sPrice} for executive or VIP travel. Your chauffeur collects you from your hotel in Stare Miasto or Kazimierz, from Kraków Główny or from Arrivals at Kraków Airport, and drops you at the door of your Prague hotel, apartment or meeting.

The fare is fixed before you travel: fuel, the A4 toll, the Czech motorway vignette, bottled water, Wi-Fi and child seats on request are all included. No early train, no change of platform, no taxi to find at Prague’s main station.

paragraphs: From a pickup near the Rynek Główny, below Wawel or at Kraków Airport in Balice, your chauffeur joins the A4 heading west. The stretch to Katowice is a toll motorway — the toll is already in your fare. Beyond Katowice the route turns south through Upper Silesia toward the Czech border near Ostrava.

The crossing is inside the Schengen Area: no routine check, no queue. Depending on traffic your chauffeur uses the motorway crossing at Gorzyczki or the older route through Cieszyn and Český Těšín. On the Czech side the D1 runs southwest across Moravia — through the Moravian Gate, past Přerov — and on via Brno or Olomouc toward Prague, entering the city from the southeast. Total distance is approximately 385 kilometres; driving time is about four hours, longer on a Friday afternoon.
Your chauffeur checks the A4 and the D1 before departure and chooses the faster line on the day. You reach Prague in time to settle in, walk the riverbank and have dinner in Malá Strana.

includedIntro: The fixed price covers everything from your Kraków pickup to your Prague drop-off: car, chauffeur, fuel, the Polish motorway tolls and the Czech vignette. Whether Prague is the next city on your tour or the start of a business week, you arrive at the door with nothing left to arrange.
inclusions: A black Mercedes — E-Class, S-Class or V-Class depending on group size and preference. Every vehicle under three years old.
A professional chauffeur — fluent English and Czech.
Fuel, the Polish A4 toll and other motorway tolls on the way, and the Czech motorway vignette. Nothing is charged on top.
Pickup at any Kraków address, Kraków Główny station, or inside Arrivals at Kraków Airport (KRK) with flight tracking.
Drop-off at the exact Prague address you give us — hotel entrance, apartment door, office or Václav Havel Airport (PRG).
Bottled water, phone charger and Wi-Fi in the rear cabin.
Child seats on request — rear-facing infant, forward-facing toddler or booster. No additional charge.
Stops on the way — Wieliczka, Auschwitz-Birkenau or Olomouc — agreed at booking.
fleetNote: All vehicles are late-model Mercedes-Benz, maintained to manufacturer standard. Child seats available on request at no charge.

journeyStops.note: Pickup from your hotel, office, Kraków Główny or Kraków Airport (KRK). At the airport your chauffeur waits inside Arrivals with your name.
The State Museum at Oświęcim lies west of Kraków, a detour from the A4. Visits need a timed entry booked in advance.
A Moravian city with a UNESCO-listed Holy Trinity Column and two fine squares, close to the route.
A lunch, a viewpoint, a meeting on the way? Tell us at booking and we plan it in.
Drop-off at any Prague address, Prague main station or Václav Havel Airport (PRG) for an onward flight.

goodToKnow.label: Border crossing
goodToKnow.value: Polish–Czech Schengen border near Ostrava (Gorzyczki or Cieszyn/Český Těšín). No routine passport check — non-EU passengers should still carry their passport and visa.

goodToKnow.label: Tolls
goodToKnow.value: The A4 toll between Kraków and Katowice, other motorway tolls on the way and the Czech vignette are all included in the quoted price.

goodToKnow.label: Airport pickup
goodToKnow.value: Give us your flight number. Your chauffeur tracks the landing at Kraków Airport and the first 60 minutes of waiting are free.

goodToKnow.label: Return transfer
goodToKnow.value: Travelling back to Kraków later? Book both directions together for a reduced rate.

dayTrip.intro: Four hours across Silesia and Moravia leaves room for one meaningful stop. These three are the ones clients ask for most.

configurations.title: Wieliczka Salt Mine
configurations.body: Start early and spend the morning underground at Wieliczka, the UNESCO salt mine just southeast of Kraków — the guided route takes around two hours. Then west on the A4 and in Prague by early evening.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial
configurations.body: Leave Kraków at 7:30 for a booked, timed-entry visit to the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum in Oświęcim. Allow three to four hours. A quiet onward drive to Prague, handled with discretion.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: Lunch in Olomouc
configurations.body: Olomouc sits close to the route through Moravia. Ninety minutes for lunch on the Upper Square beside the Holy Trinity Column, then about two and a half hours to your Prague door.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

dayTrip.footnote: Stops are planned at booking and priced by the extra time and distance — tell us where you would like to stop and we confirm a firm quote before you book. A short coffee or rest stop on the way is always included.

chauffeurNarrative: Your chauffeur meets you at the door of your Kraków hotel — in Kazimierz or the Old Town that sometimes means a short walk to where cars may stop, and they carry the bags for it. At Kraków Airport they wait inside Arrivals with your name.

Four hours is a good stretch to work, rest or talk. Your chauffeur reads which one you want. If you would like advice on Prague — where to walk first, which hotel entrance to use, how to get to the Castle before the crowds — they are the right person to ask.
Water, charger and Wi-Fi are in the back. A coffee near Ostrava or a pause in Olomouc is yours for the asking. In Prague your luggage goes into the hotel with you.

items.title: Every toll already counted
items.body: The A4 toll, the Czech vignette, fuel and the chauffeur’s time are in the fare. What you see at booking is what you pay.

items.title: No long train, no changes
items.body: Your bags go in the boot at your Kraków hotel and come out at your Prague address. No station at either end.

items.title: A company from Prague
items.body: Prestigo is based in Prague and runs its own Mercedes fleet. Your chauffeur knows the city you are arriving in — the one-way streets, the hotel drop-off points, the quickest way across the river.

faqs.q: How long does a private transfer from Kraków to Prague take?
faqs.a: About four hours door to door: the A4 west past Katowice, across the border near Ostrava and the D1 through Moravia into Prague. Friday afternoon traffic can add 20–30 minutes.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi or chauffeur from Kraków to Prague?
faqs.a: A fixed fare from €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers, €{vPrice} in the V-Class for up to 6, or €{sPrice} in the S-Class. Fuel, the Polish motorway tolls, the Czech vignette and the chauffeur’s time are included — per car, not per person.

faqs.q: Can you pick me up at Kraków Airport and drive me straight to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Give us your flight number when you book. Your chauffeur tracks the landing, waits inside Arrivals at Kraków Airport with your name and drives you directly to your Prague address — no need to go into Kraków first.

faqs.q: Is a private transfer better than the train from Kraków to Prague?
faqs.a: Direct trains run, but the daytime journey takes considerably longer than the drive, and the other option is the overnight sleeper. For a solo traveller with light bags the train is the cheaper choice. A private car is door to door, leaves when you want and costs the same for one passenger or three.

faqs.q: Can we stop on the way from Kraków to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Wieliczka, the Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial and Olomouc are the most common stops. Tell us at booking and we include the stop in a fixed quote. A short coffee or rest break is always included.

faqs.q: Do I need my passport between Poland and the Czech Republic?
faqs.a: Both countries are in the Schengen Area, so there is no routine border control. Carry your passport or EU ID card anyway — spot checks happen, and non-EU travellers must have their documents with them.

relatedRoutesIntro: Kraków to Prague is often one leg of a Central European tour. Clients arriving from Ostrava, Wrocław or Warsaw book the same way — one car, one fixed fare, drop-off at the door in Prague.
